title: Executive sales dashboard
problem: Leadership got sales numbers two weeks late in emailed spreadsheets.
approach: Star-schema model, DAX measures for YoY and margin, and row-level security per region.
result: Daily refresh; the weekly reporting meeting was cut from 2 hours to 30 minutes.

title: Subscription retention analysis
problem: A SaaS company did not know why customers cancelled after month three.
approach: Cohort retention curves, feature-usage correlation and a churn-driver memo.
result: Identified onboarding gap; a fix lifted month-3 retention from 61% to 69%.

title: Modern data stack migration
problem: Metrics differed between teams because each had its own spreadsheets.
approach: Moved reporting to a warehouse with tested, documented models and scheduled runs.
result: 48 dbt models with 160 tests; 'which number is right' tickets dropped to near zero.

title: Website funnel and GA4 audit
problem: An online shop saw traffic grow but sales stay flat.
approach: Fixed event tracking, built a funnel report and found a broken mobile checkout step.
result: Mobile conversion rose from 1.1% to 1.9% after the fix.

title: Pricing A/B test analysis
problem: A startup wanted to raise prices without losing sign-ups.
approach: Designed a 3-arm experiment with power analysis and sequential monitoring.
result: Shipped the +15% arm: revenue per visitor +9% with no significant drop in conversion (p=0.41).

title: Inventory demand forecast in Excel
problem: Pharmacies ran out of seasonal medicines every winter.
approach: Seasonal forecasting model in Excel with Power Query refresh, usable by non-technical staff.

title: Marketing attribution in BigQuery
problem: An agency could not tell clients which channels drove sales.
approach: Built position-based attribution from raw GA4 export and ad-platform costs.
result: Reallocated 20% of spend; client ROAS improved from 2.1 to 2.8.

title: Customer segmentation for loyalty
problem: One-size-fits-all loyalty emails got poor engagement.
approach: RFM features and clustering into 6 segments with personas and playbooks.
result: Email click-through up 43% after segment-specific campaigns.

title: Hospital operations dashboard
problem: Bed occupancy was tracked on a whiteboard.
approach: Live occupancy, length-of-stay and discharge forecasts for 6 wards.

title: Automated reporting pipeline
problem: An analyst spent every Monday morning copying numbers into slides.
approach: Scheduled pipeline loads data, runs checks and refreshes self-serve dashboards.
result: Saved ~6 hours per week; zero missed reports in 6 months.

title: Survey statistics report in R
problem: A school network needed a rigorous analysis of a 4,000-respondent parent survey.
approach: Weighted estimates, regression on satisfaction drivers and a plain-language report.
result: Board adopted 3 of 4 recommendations; report cited in the annual plan.

title: Self-serve analytics with Metabase
problem: Product managers waited days for analysts to answer simple questions.
approach: Curated models, a metrics glossary and training for 20 PMs.
result: Ad-hoc analyst requests down 50% in two months.

title: Interactive Streamlit KPI explorer
problem: Credit risk team wanted to slice approval rates without writing SQL.
approach: Internal web app with filters, cohort charts and CSV export on top of the warehouse.
result: Used daily by 14 analysts; replaced 9 static reports.

title: Revenue forecasting for a marketplace
problem: A marketplace needed GMV projections for a fundraising deck.
approach: Built a hierarchical forecast by category with scenario bands.
result: Actuals landed within the 80% band for 5 of 6 months.

title: Data cleaning and ETL for a CRM merge
problem: Two merged agencies had 60k duplicated, inconsistent contact records.
approach: Fuzzy de-duplication, standardisation rules and a reviewed merge file.
result: 60k records reduced to 38k clean contacts with a 99% match-review accuracy.
